To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The effects of contextual stimuli on evaluative judgments depend on when the contextual stimuli are processed.
the effect of contextual contrast depends on how fast a judge makes a decision.

(a) the effect of contextual information on trait evaluation depends on the order of processing of trait and context, (b) the order of processing depends on the rate of judgment, and (c) the order of trait and context processing is determined by the rate of processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of context in the formation of judgments of persons and events.
the question of whether or not the context in which judgments are made affects the valence of the judgments.
how the social context affects the formation of evaluative judgments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
contextual contrast effects occur in evaluative judgments, but the level at which they operate is a function of the speed with which impressions are formed.
the present research has demonstrated that contextual contrast is an active and important component of impression formation.
the results are consistent with the preintegration model of contextual contrast.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the context in which people evaluate targets affects the way in which they judge those targets.
contrast effects are a function of the processing level of the subject and the processing level of contrast.
contrast effects are a function of both the processing level of the subject and the processing level of contextual stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should not be too quick to dismiss the possibility that the way people process information in a given situation is influenced by the speed with which they make their judgments.
the context in which a judgment is made is very important.
people are not always rational in the ways they evaluate information.
